title: Italicized Displayed Verse

illustrates.quote: Omit font attributes when the entire section of displayed material is emphasized.

blocks.text: Many upper-class people from Judah were sent to Babylonia in exile, the memory of which is still evoked in the stirring words of Psalm 137:

blocks.features: Four-line displayed verse, entirely italicized in print; per 9.2.3b the italic font attribute is omitted in braille since the whole displayed section is emphasized -- each verse line at the adjusted left margin (cell 3), runovers at cell 5, per this section's own 'multiple displayed sentences treated as a list' pattern (9.2.2e).
items: By the rivers of Babylon, we sat and wept when we remembered Zion …
How can we sing the songs of the Lord while in a foreign land?
If I forgot you, O Jerusalem, may my right hand forget its skill.
May my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth if I do not remember you, if I do not consider Jerusalem my highest joy.

blocks.text: But the Babylonian captivity of the people of Judah did not last.

print.notes: Direct worked example of 9.2.3b: no italic/emphasis indicator is used anywhere in the braille verse lines even though every word of the verse is italicized in print.
print.printFeatures: Plain (unboxed) narrative text; the four-line verse is set in italics and indented as a block quotation.

braille.notes: Numbered lines 6-21 in the source (a genuine excerpt). Field width 5, stripped. Lines 1-3 (source 6-8): lead-in paragraph at cell 1. Line 4 (9): blank. resolution: A and B transcribed identical `braille.lines`, verified byte-for-byte against lines 6914-6929 after stripping the 5-character line-number field (the '(Return to Text)' line 6930 excluded). `illustrates.rule` narrowed to 9.2.3.b specifically (B quoted the whole of 9.2.3 including clause a; A cited b alone) since the sample shows the WHOLE passage emphasized, clause b's specific case, not clause a's partial-emphasis case. Structural choice: A recorded the verse as a 'quote' block carrying an `items` array (poem-like); B flattened it into one 'quote' block's `text` (joining the four lines with spaces, losing the line-per-line structure). Resolved to A's `items` structure: the agreed braille shows each verse line independently satisfying the cell-3-first/cell-5-runover pattern (measured directly, matching this section's own 'displayed sentences as a list' convention, 9.2.2e) rather than one continuously-wrapped paragraph, so a flat joined `text` would lose the very line-per-line structure the braille exhibits; kept as `kind:'list'` (not 'quote'+items) for buildModel9's consistency with example-9-4's identical list-of-displayed-sentences pattern.
